Core resistome: 23 genes found in all libraries; 35 genes in ≥90% of libraries

extraction_warnings: Paper reports study-level and cohort-level data stratified by travel destination, not individual sample-level data. No sample identifiers or per-participant rows are provided; granularity is best described as study_level with travel destination subgroups.
Individual subject_id and sample_id values are not provided in the paper. Sequence data are available under ENA accession PRJEB7369.
Sex is reported as aggregate (74% female) but not per individual.
Age is reported as range (23–34 years) not individual values.
Field 'samples' array populated as empty because paper does not provide per-sample metadata rows; only cohort-level or subgroup-level summaries are available.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

This is an observational microbiome travel study of healthy adult exchange students, not a clinical treatment trial. Most schema fields (neonatal, obstetric, tumor staging, disease response) are not applicable.
Gender distribution reported as 74% females (26/35) but sex-specific data not stratified per individual participant.
Study has subgroup data by travel destination (Central Africa n=17 vs Indian peninsula n=18) but extraction performed at study_level as requested by schema context.
Antimalarial agents used by participants may have had antibacterial effects, which is discussed but not definitively linked to resistance gene changes.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
No tumor-related or survival data present; fields disease_response_os, tumor_size_measurement, and tumor_size_residual_measurement are not applicable to this microbiome study.
No ECOG performance status reported; this is not an oncology or clinical severity assessment study.
Biomarker values span multiple measurement types (fold-changes, counts, proportions); ensure downstream harmonization accounts for unit heterogeneity.
ESBL phenotype vs. metagenomics discordance noted: CTX-M-15 genes detected in culture isolates were often missed by metagenomic sequencing despite high depth.
No per-sample rows from the article's own tables; falling back to the SRA/ENA run manifest (1 table(s)).
